patch_description: The best-performing prior program (combined_score 0.76) used a scipy Powell optimization over softmax-barycentric logits with a smooth softmin objective — the current stochastic-climb version regressed to 0.51. The key weakness of that softmin approach is gradient dilution: with 165 triples, most are far above the minimum and contribute negligible but noisy signal, so Powell wastes iterations. I restore the scipy/softmax framework and, per the recommendation, replace the uniform softmin over all 165 triples with a top-k (k=20) temperature-annealed log-sum-exp over only the smallest areas, using the numerically robust `a.min()` shift. Because only the ~20 binding constraints matter, the objective surface is far better conditioned for Powell, and each restart converges faster and to better minima. I keep two annealing temperatures and 4 deterministic starts to stay within runtime budget, and retain the existing `_polish` as a cheap final feasibility-aware touch-up that can only help (results are kept only if they improve the true min area).
